title: Reactions of Acids with Metal Oxides

content.text: Reactions of Acids with Metal Oxides
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Write equations for reactions between acids and metal oxides
Explain why these are neutralisation reactions
Use these reactions to make salts
- they neutralise acids. When a metal oxide reacts with an acid, a salt and water are produced. This is a key method for preparing salts in the laboratory.
This IS a neutralisation reaction (water is formed).
O²⁻ acts as a base, accepting H⁺ ions
[DIAGRAM: Black powder (CuO) being added to acid, forming blue solution (CuSO₄)]
Black copper oxide powder is added to warm acid
The solution turns blue (copper sulfate solution)
When excess oxide is added, some black solid remains
Using This Reaction to Make Salts
Warm the acid gently in a beaker
Add metal oxide a little at a time, stirring
Continue until oxide stops dissolving (excess remains)
Evaporate the filtrate to crystallise the salt
To ensure all the acid has reacted
Unreacted oxide can be easily filtered off
Ensures the salt solution is not contaminated with acid
Write the equation for the reaction of zinc oxide with dilute hydrochloric acid. Include state symbols.
Describe what you would observe when black copper oxide is added to warm dilute sulfuric acid.
The mixture warms up (reaction is exothermic)
Effervescence is NOT observed (no gas is produced)
Explain why the reaction of a metal oxide with an acid is called neutralisation.
They can accept H⁺ ions from the acid
The oxide ion (O²⁻) reacts with H⁺: O²⁻ + 2H⁺ → H₂O
The H⁺ ions are removed (acid is neutralised)
Products are salt + water (typical of neutralisation)
A student wants to make pure magnesium sulfate crystals from magnesium oxide and sulfuric acid. Describe the method.
Pour dilute sulfuric acid into a beaker and warm gently
Add magnesium oxide powder, stirring continuously
Keep adding oxide until no more dissolves (excess remains)
Filter the mixture to remove excess magnesium oxide
Pour the filtrate (magnesium sulfate solution) into an evaporating basin
Heat gently to evaporate some water
Filter to collect crystals and dry with filter paper
Expecting bubbles when metal oxide reacts with acid
No gas is produced - this is NOT the metal + acid reaction
Forgetting that metal oxides are bases
Metal oxides ARE bases (they neutralise acids)
Write the general word equation for the reaction of a metal oxide with an acid. (1 mark)
a) Copper oxide + hydrochloric acid (2 marks)
b) Magnesium oxide + sulfuric acid (2 marks)
c) Iron(III) oxide + hydrochloric acid (2 marks)
Describe what you would observe when magnesium oxide powder is added to warm dilute hydrochloric acid. (3 marks)
Explain why adding copper oxide to sulfuric acid is a neutralisation reaction. (3 marks)
Describe how you would prepare a pure dry sample of zinc sulfate starting from zinc oxide and dilute sulfuric acid. (6 marks)
Why is excess metal oxide added when preparing a salt by this method? (2 marks)
A compound of a metal with oxygen; acts as a base
A substance that neutralises an acid
The liquid that passes through a filter
More than enough to react with all of another substance
No gas is produced (unlike metal + acid)
Observations: solid dissolves, solution may change colour, warms up
Add excess oxide to warm acid
Colour changes help identify the reaction (e.g., black CuO → blue CuSO₄)
